question:
The proclamation of which Act by the King of England in 1773 paved the way for the establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta?

[SSC CHSL 2024]
options:
Pitt’s India Act

Indian Councils Act

Regulating Act 

Charter Act
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Regulating Act

Explanation:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was passed by King George III of England to regulate the administrative and political affairs of the British East India Company. This act led to the establishment of the Supreme Court at Calcutta in 1774, consisting of a Chief Justice and three other judges. This court had jurisdiction over British subjects and Company employees in India.

Extra Facts:
☛ The Regulating Act, 1773, designated the Governor of Bengal as the 'Governor-General' and created a 4-member Executive Council to assist him.
☛ It marked the first step by the British Parliament to establish control over the East India Company.
☛ The first Chief Justice of the Supreme Court was Sir Elijah Impey.

☛ In which year was the Regulating Act passed? → 1773
☛ Which act created the post of Governor-General in India? → Regulating Act, 1773
☛ Which act initiated British Parliament's control over the East India Company? → Regulating Act, 1773

question:
The British Parliament introduced the Indian High Courts Act in which year?

[SSC CGL 2024]
options: 1860
1861
1859
1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1861

Explanation:
The British Parliament introduced the Indian High Courts Act, 1861 in 1861. This act aimed to establish High Courts in India, leading to the formation of High Courts in Calcutta, Bombay, and Madras. The act was introduced to strengthen and reform the Indian judicial system under British rule. It abolished the Supreme Courts and Sadar Diwani Adalats, replacing them with High Courts.

Extra Facts:
☛ The first High Court in India was established in Calcutta in 1862, followed by Bombay and Madras.
☛ The Indian High Courts Act, 1861 laid the foundation for the modernization of the Indian judiciary.
☛ Currently, India has 25 High Courts, some of which have jurisdiction over multiple states.

☛ How many High Courts are there in India? → 25
☛ Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for High Courts? → Article 214
☛ Who appoints the judges of the High Court? → The President
☛ Which is the newest High Court in India? → Andhra Pradesh High Court (2019)

question:
All the _______ countries likely to have Constitution.

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: communist
democratic
oligarchic
totalitarian
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is democratic

Explanation:
All democratic countries have their own constitution because the constitution is the foundation of democracy. It limits the powers of the government and protects the rights of citizens. The Indian Constitution, which is the world's largest written constitution, ensures democratic values. Articles 1 to 4 of the Constitution declare India as a 'Federal Democratic Republic'. Democracy cannot be imagined without a constitution, as it provides fundamental rights to citizens and regulates the functions of the government.

Extra Facts:
The Indian Constitution was adopted on 26th November 1949 and came into effect on 26th January 1950. It consists of 22 parts, 395 articles, and 12 schedules. The Preamble of the Constitution begins with the words 'We, the People of India', which reflects the spirit of democracy. Article 326 of the Constitution provides for adult suffrage, which is a crucial pillar of democracy.

☛ Which article provides for adult suffrage in India? → Article 326

question_hi:
सभी_______देशों का अपना संविधान होता है।

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: साम्यवादी
लोकतांत्रिक
कुलीनतंत्रीय
सर्वसत्तात्मक
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है लोकतांत्रिक

Explanation:
सभी लोकतांत्रिक देशों का अपना संविधान होता है क्योंकि संविधान लोकतंत्र का मूल आधार है। यह सरकार की शक्तियों को सीमित करता है और नागरिकों के अधिकारों की रक्षा करता है। भारत का संविधान, जो दुनिया का सबसे बड़ा लिखित संविधान है, लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों को सुनिश्चित करता है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 1 से 4 में भारत को एक 'संघीय लोकतांत्रिक गणराज्य' घोषित किया गया है। संविधान के बिना लोकतंत्र की कल्पना नहीं की जा सकती, क्योंकि यह नागरिकों को मौलिक अधिकार प्रदान करता है और सरकार के कार्यों को नियंत्रित करता है।

Extra Facts:
भारतीय संविधान को 26 नवंबर 1949 को अपनाया गया और 26 जनवरी 1950 को लागू किया गया। इसमें 22 भाग, 395 अनुच्छेद और 12 अनुसूचियाँ हैं। संविधान की प्रस्तावना में 'हम भारत के लोग' शब्दों का प्रयोग किया गया है, जो लोकतंत्र की भावना को दर्शाता है। संविधान के अनुच्छेद 326 में वयस्क मताधिकार का प्रावधान है, जो लोकतंत्र का एक महत्वपूर्ण स्तंभ है।

question:
Which act allows the government to confiscate the assets of newspaper in case of publishing anything “objectionable”?

[SSC CGL 2022]
options: Ilbert Act, 1883
Vernacular Press Act, 1878
Media Act, 1883
Newspaper Act, 1855
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Vernacular Press Act, 1878

Explanation:
The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was introduced by the British government to regulate newspapers published in Indian languages (vernacular languages). Under this act, the government was empowered to confiscate the assets of a newspaper if it published anything deemed "objectionable" and could shut down the press. The primary objective was to suppress criticism of the British rule and the Indian freedom movement. This act was also known as the 'Gagging Act'.

Extra Facts:
- This act was passed during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton (1876-1880).
- It caused widespread resentment among Indian nationalists, leading to its repeal in 1882 by Lord Ripon.
- The act applied only to vernacular (local language) presses, exempting English-language newspapers.

☛ Which Viceroy implemented the Vernacular Press Act? → Lord Lytton
☛ In which year was the Vernacular Press Act repealed? → 1882
☛ In which year was the Ilbert Bill introduced? → 1883
☛ Which act restricted the freedom of the Indian press? → Vernacular Press Act, 1878
question_hi:

[SSC CGL 2022]
options_hi: इल्बर्ट एक्ट, 1883
वर्नाक्यूलर प्रेस एक्ट, 1878
मीडिया एक्ट 1883
समाचार पत्र अधिनियम, 1855
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है वर्नाक्यूलर प्रेस एक्ट, 1878

Explanation:
वर्नाक्यूलर प्रेस एक्ट, 1878 ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा भारतीय भाषाओं (स्थानीय भाषाओं) में प्रकाशित होने वाले समाचार पत्रों को नियंत्रित करने के लिए लाया गया था। इस अधिनियम के तहत, सरकार को यह अधिकार दिया गया था कि यदि कोई समाचार पत्र 'आपत्तिजनक' सामग्री प्रकाशित करता है, तो वह उसकी संपत्ति जब्त कर सकती है और प्रेस को बंद कर सकती है। इसका मुख्य उद्देश्य भारतीय स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन की आलोचना को दबाना था। इस अधिनियम को 'गैगिंग एक्ट' भी कहा जाता था।

Extra Facts:
- यह अधिनियम लॉर्ड लिटन के वायसराय काल (1876-1880) में पारित किया गया था।
- इस अधिनियम ने भारतीय राष्ट्रवादियों में व्यापक आक्रोश पैदा किया, जिसके कारण इसे 1882 में लॉर्ड रिपन द्वारा निरस्त कर दिया गया।
- यह अधिनियम केवल स्थानीय भाषाओं के प्रेस पर लागू होता था, अंग्रेजी भाषा के प्रेस को इससे छूट दी गई थी।

question:
The Charter Act of 1813 extended the East India Company's rule in India to another_________ years.

[SSC MTS 2022]
options:
15

5

20

10
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 20

Explanation:
The Charter Act of 1813 was a significant legislation passed by the British Parliament, which extended the East India Company's rule in India for another 20 years. This act abolished the Company's trade monopoly (except for trade with China and tea) and allowed Christian missionaries to propagate their religion in India. It marked a turning point in British rule in India, as it allocated funds for education and social reforms.

Extra Facts:
☛ The Charter Act of 1813 allocated 1 lakh rupees annually for the promotion of education in India.
☛ It permitted Christian missionaries☛ This act preceded the Charter Act of 1833, which completely ended the Company's trade monopoly.

☛ What is the Charter Act of 1833 known for? → Completely ending the Company's trade monopoly

बंगाल राज्य कैदी विनियमन (बंगाल विनियमन III) को 1818 में पारित किया गया था। यह एक औपनिवेशिक कानून था जिसे ब्रिटिश सरकार ने भारतीय स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों और राजनीतिक कैदियों को बिना मुकदमा चलाए नजरबंद करने के लिए बनाया था। इस विनियम के तहत, ब्रिटिश अधिकारियों को यह अधिकार दिया गया था कि वे किसी भी व्यक्ति को 'राज्य के खिलाफ' गतिविधियों में शामिल होने के संदेह में गिरफ्तार कर सकते थे और उसे बिना किसी न्यायिक प्रक्रिया के जेल में रख सकते थे। यह कानून भारतीय राष्ट्रीय आंदोलन के दौरान अक्सर विवादास्पद रहा और स्वतंत्रता सेनानियों के खिलाफ दमनकारी उपाय के रूप में प्रयोग किया गया।

Extra Facts:

question:
Although there was a category of industries left to the private sector, the sector was kept under state control through a system of licenses. No new industry was allowed unless a license was obtained from the government. The above lines are about which of the following ?

[SSC GD 2022]
options: IPR-1956
IPR-1952
IPR-1951
IPR-1958
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is IPR-1956

Explanation:
The above lines refer to the Industrial Policy Resolution 1956 (IPR-1956). This was India's second industrial policy, based on the principle of the 'Socialist Pattern of Society'. Under this policy, industries were classified into three categories:
1. Schedule A (17 industries) – Reserved exclusively for the state.
2. Schedule B (12 industries) – State and private sector could jointly operate, but new industries required government licenses.
3. Schedule C – Remaining industries open to the private sector, but subject to licensing.
The main objective of this policy was to promote a mixed economy, where both public and private sectors played a role.

Extra Facts:
- IPR-1956 was drafted based on the Mahalanobis Model and the Second Five-Year Plan (1956-61).
- This policy initiated the License Raj, leading to increased corruption and bureaucracy.
- The 1991 New Industrial Policy (Liberalization) abolished this licensing system.
- Article 19(1)(g) (Freedom of trade and business) was impacted by IPR-1956 as the government controlled industries.

☛ What caused the 'License Raj' in India? → IPR-1956

question_hi:
यद्यपि निजी क्षेत्र में आने वाले उद्योगों का भी एक वर्ग था, लेकिन इस क्षेत्रक को लाइसेंस पद्धति के माध्यम से राज्य के नियंत्रण में रखा गया था। सरकार से लाइसेंस प्राप्त किए बिना किसी भी नए उद्योग की अनुमति नहीं दी जाती थी। उपरोक्त पंक्तियाँ निम्नलिखित में से किसके बारे में हैं ?

[SSC GD 2022]
options_hi: IPR-1956
IPR-1952
IPR-1951
IPR-1958
solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है IPR-1956

Explanation:
उपरोक्त पंक्तियाँ औद्योगिक नीति प्रस्ताव 1956 (IPR-1956) के बारे में हैं। यह नीति भारत की दूसरी औद्योगिक नीति थी, जिसे 'सोशलिस्ट पैटर्न ऑफ सोसाइटी' के सिद्धांत पर आधारित किया गया था। इस नीति के तहत उद्योगों को तीन श्रेणियों में बाँटा गया था:
1. श्रेणी A (17 उद्योग) – जिन पर राज्य का पूर्ण स्वामित्व होगा।
2. श्रेणी B (12 उद्योग) – जिनमें राज्य और निजी क्षेत्र साझेदारी कर सकते थे, लेकिन नए उद्योगों के लिए सरकारी लाइसेंस अनिवार्य था।
3. श्रेणी C – शेष उद्योग, जो निजी क्षेत्र के लिए खुले थे, लेकिन लाइसेंस पद्धति लागू थी।
इस नीति का मुख्य उद्देश्य मिश्रित अर्थव्यवस्था को बढ़ावा देना था, जहाँ सार्वजनिक और निजी क्षेत्र दोनों की भूमिका हो।

Extra Facts:
- IPR-1956 को महालनोबिस मॉडल और द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना (1956-61) के आधार पर तैयार किया गया था।
- इस नीति ने लाइसेंस राज की शुरुआत की, जिसके कारण भ्रष्टाचार और नौकरशाही में वृद्धि हुई।
- 1991 की नई औद्योगिक नीति (उदारीकरण) ने इस लाइसेंस पद्धति को समाप्त कर दिया।
- अनुच्छेद 19(1)(g) (व्यापार और व्यवसाय की स्वतंत्रता) पर IPR-1956 का प्रभाव पड़ा, क्योंकि सरकार ने उद्योगों पर नियंत्रण रखा।

question:
In which year the Municipal Corporation was established in Calcutta by a royal charter?

[RRC GROUP D]
options: 1726
1736
1687
1688
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1726

Explanation:
In 1726, the British government established the Municipal Corporation in Calcutta (now Kolkata) through a Royal Charter. This marked the beginning of municipal administration in India. The charter also set up similar corporations in Madras (now Chennai) and Bombay (now Mumbai), known as 'Mayor’s Courts'. This was the first attempt by the British to develop local self-governing structures in India.

Extra Facts:
☛ In 1687-88, the first municipal body, the 'Madras Municipal Corporation', was established in Madras (Chennai), but it was not formally created by a Royal Charter.
☛ The 1726 Charter was significant for both judicial and civil administration as it laid the foundation for the British legal system in India.
☛ Later, post-1850, municipal administration in India was further strengthened, leading to Lord Ripon’s Resolution of 1882, often called the 'Magna Carta of Local Self-Government'.

In which of the following years was the interim Government formed at the Centre ?

[SSC GD 2024]
options: 1916

1946
1936
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1946

Explanation:
The Interim Government at the Centre was formed on 2 September 1946. This government was established during the final phase of British India and was led by Jawaharlal Nehru. It was formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946), which aimed to establish a constitutional framework before granting independence to India. The Interim Government included both the Congress and the Muslim League, though the League later withdrew due to disagreements. This government functioned until 15 August 1947, when India gained independence and a new government was formed.

Extra Facts:
- Lord Wavell was the Viceroy when the Interim Government was formed.
- The government had 12 members, including 3 representatives from the Muslim League (who later resigned).
- The Constituent Assembly of India was formed based on the recommendations of the Cabinet Mission, which drafted the Indian Constitution.
- The Interim Government played a crucial role in managing the Partition and Independence process.

question:
Which among the following Acts discarded the 'dyarchy’ system at the provincial level and allowed for the emergence of popularly elected provincial legislatures?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Charter Act, 1793
Montague-Chelmsford Reform (Government of India Act), 1919
(Government of India Act), 1935
Pitt's India Act, 1784
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 abolished the 'dyarchy' system at the provincial level and promoted provincial autonomy. This act granted more powers to provincial legislatures and introduced provisions for their popular election. It was a significant step by the British government towards constitutional reforms in India, strengthening provincial self-governance. The act also introduced a federal structure, though it was never fully implemented.

Extra Facts:
The dyarchy system was first introduced under the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montague-Chelmsford Reforms), which divided provincial subjects into 'reserved' and 'transferred' categories. The 1935 Act abolished this system and expanded provincial autonomy. Many provisions of this act were later incorporated into the Indian Constitution, making it a key foundation for India's constitutional framework.

question:
How many members (elected and nominated) were there in the Council of State under the Government of India Act 1919 passed by the Parliament of the United Kingdom to expand participation of Indians in the government of India ?

options: 70
50
75
60
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 60

Explanation:
Under the Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms), the Council of State consisted of a total of 60 members, out of which 33 were elected and 27 were nominated. This act was a significant step towards constitutional reforms in India, introducing the Dyarchy system at the provincial level and dividing the central legislature into two houses—the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly. The aim was to provide limited participation of Indians in governance, though real power remained with the British government.

Extra Facts:
- The Government of India Act, 1919 provided for 145 members (103 elected + 42 nominated) in the Central Legislative Assembly.
- It classified provincial subjects into 'Reserved' and 'Transferred' categories, with Indian ministers handling transferred subjects.
- The act came into force in 1921 and remained effective until the 1935 Act.

question:
What was the Government of India Act 1935 based on?

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: The acceptance of the independence of india
The acceptance of the idea of a constituent assembly to draft a constitution
The principle of federation and parliamentary system
The principle of session of the British India provinces
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The principle of federation and parliamentary system

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1935 was primarily based on the principle of federation and parliamentary system. This act was introduced by the British government to bring constitutional reforms in India. It established a division of powers between the Centre and provinces, adopting a federal structure. Additionally, it introduced a parliamentary system where the executive was responsible to the legislature. This act became a significant foundation for the Indian Constitution, especially regarding federal structure, governor's powers, and emergency provisions.

Extra Facts:
- The Government of India Act 1935 is often called the blueprint of the Indian Constitution as many of its provisions were incorporated into the Constitution.
- It granted autonomy to provinces but retained special powers for the Governor-General and Governors.
- The provision for establishing a Federal Court was made in this act, which later became the basis for the Supreme Court of India.

question:
By which of the following acts was a bicameral legislature introduced in India at the center level?

[SSC CGL 2023]
options: Indian councils Act of 1861
Regulating Act of 1773
Government of India Act of 1919
Government of India Act of 1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act, 1919

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced a bicameral legislature at the central level in India. This act divided the Central Legislature into two houses: the Council of State (Upper House) and the Central Legislative Assembly (Lower House). Inspired by the British parliamentary system, this reform laid the foundation for a federal structure in India. The act also introduced Dyarchy (Dual Government) at the provincial level, where certain subjects were transferred to Indian ministers while others remained under British control.

Extra Facts:
The Government of India Act, 1935 further developed the 1919 Act and strengthened the federal structure. It provided for the establishment of a Federal Court and increased provincial autonomy. The 1935 Act is considered a major source of the Indian Constitution, as many of its provisions, such as the federal structure, Governor’s office, and emergency provisions, were incorporated into the Constitution of India.

question:
The British parliament transferred the powers of the East India company to the British crown in _______ .

[SSC MTS 2022]

1919

Explanation:
The British Parliament passed the Government of India Act, 1858, which transferred all administrative and political powers of the East India Company to the British Crown. question:
Which among the following Acts introduced the Diarchy, i.e., rule of two which means executive councillors and popular ministers?

[SSC MTS 2022]
options: Charter Act, 1813
Government of India Act, 1858
Montague-Chelmsford Reform (Government of India Act), 1919
Indian Council Act, 1861
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Montague-Chelmsford Reform (Government of India Act), 1919

Explanation:
The Montague-Chelmsford Reforms (Government of India Act, 1919) introduced the system of Diarchy in India. Under this act, provincial governments were divided into two parts: Reserved Subjects (controlled by the Governor and his Executive Council) and Transferred Subjects (controlled by elected Indian ministers). This system failed due to a lack of coordination between the two branches and excessive powers vested in the Governor.

Extra Facts:
- Diarchy was abolished by the Government of India Act, 1935, which promoted provincial autonomy.
- The 1919 Act introduced a Bicameral Legislature at the center, consisting of the Council of State and the Central Legislative Assembly.
- It introduced direct elections but with limited franchise.

question:
Consider the following statement about the Government of India Act, 1935.
1. This act was enacted by the British Parliament.
2. This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma Government.

Select the correct statement(s) using the code given below.

[SSC MTS 2023]
options: Both 1 and 2
1, 2 and 3
Both 2 and 3
Both 1 and 3
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Both 1 and 2

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 was enacted by the British Parliament (Statement 1 correct). This Act was divided into two separate acts for India and Burma (now Myanmar) (Statement 2 correct). However, the Act came into force on 1 April 1937, not 1 April 1935 (Statement 3 incorrect). This Act introduced provincial autonomy and established a dyarchy at the center, which became a foundation for the Indian Constitution.

Extra Facts:
The Government of India Act, 1935 is the largest source of the Indian Constitution, with around 250 provisions incorporated into it. This Act established the Federal Court, which later became the Supreme Court of India. It granted more autonomy to provinces and expanded suffrage, though it remained limited.

question:
Government of India Act, 1935 introduced

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: Dyrarchy
Provincial autonomy
Self- autonomy
Union territories
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Provincial autonomy

Explanation:
The Government of India Act, 1935 introduced provincial autonomy. This act was brought by the British government to introduce constitutional reforms in India. Under this act, provinces were given more independence from the center and the authority to make decisions on their internal matters. The act also laid the foundation for a federal structure, though it was never fully implemented. This act became an important basis for the framing of the Indian Constitution.

Extra Facts:
The Government of India Act, 1935 had a total of 321 sections and 10 schedules. The act also provided for the establishment of a Federal Court, which later became the basis for the Supreme Court of India. It granted more powers to provincial legislatures and expanded the franchise, though it was still limited. This act is the largest source of the Indian Constitution, with many of its provisions being adopted.

भारत सरकार अधिनियम, 1935 ने प्रांतीय स्वायत्तता की व्यवस्था को पेश किया। यह अधिनियम ब्रिटिश सरकार द्वारा भारत में संवैधानिक सुधारों के लिए लाया गया था। इस अधिनियम के तहत प्रांतों को केंद्र से अधिक स्वतंत्रता दी गई और उन्हें अपने आंतरिक मामलों में स्वयं निर्णय लेने का अधिकार मिला। इस अधिनियम ने संघीय ढांचे की भी शुरुआत की, हालांकि यह पूरी तरह से लागू नहीं हो पाया। यह अधिनियम भारतीय संविधान के निर्माण में एक महत्वपूर्ण आधार बना।

question:
The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment in the year 2015 notified that every year ____ will be celebrated as the ‘Constitution Day’ to promote Constitutional values among citizens.

[NTPC CBT 2]
options: 26 January
26 December
26 November
26 June
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 26 November

Explanation:
26 November is celebrated as 'Constitution Day' in India to commemorate the adoption of the Indian Constitution by the Constituent Assembly on this day in 1949. The Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950, celebrated as Republic Day. The Union Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment declared this day as Constitution Day in 2015, coinciding with the 125th birth anniversary of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the chief architect of the Indian Constitution.

Extra Facts:
- 26 January is celebrated as 'Republic Day' because the Constitution came into force on this day in 1950.
- The Constituent Assembly took 2 years, 11 months, and 18 days to draft the Constitution.
- Dr. B.R. Ambedkar is known as the 'Father of the Indian Constitution'.

solution_hi:
हल: सही उत्तर है 26 नवंबर

Explanation:
26 नवंबर को भारत में 'संविधान दिवस' (Constitution Day) के रूप में मनाया जाता है। यह दिन भारतीय संविधान सभा द्वारा संविधान को अंगीकृत (adopt) किए जाने की याद में मनाया जाता है। 26 नवंबर, 1949 को संविधान सभा ने भारतीय संविधान को पारित किया था, जो 26 जनवरी, 1950 को लागू हुआ। केंद्रीय सामाजिक न्याय और अधिकारिता मंत्रालय ने 2015 में इस दिन को संविधान दिवस के रूप में घोषित किया, जो डॉ. भीमराव अंबेडकर की 125वीं जयंती के अवसर पर था।

Extra Facts:
- 26 जनवरी को 'गणतंत्र दिवस' के रूप में मनाया जाता है, क्योंकि इस दिन 1950 में भारतीय संविधान लागू हुआ था।

- डॉ. बी.आर. अंबेडकर को 'भारतीय संविधान का जनक' (Father of the Indian Constitution) कहा जाता है।

question:
The law that permitted widows to remarry (Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act) was passed in the year:

[RRB NTPC CBT]
options: 1854
1856
1855
1858
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 1856

Explanation:
The Hindu Widows’ Remarriage Act, 1856 was passed during the reign of Lord Dalhousie in British India. This law aimed to grant Hindu widows the legal right to remarry by freeing them from social stigma and restrictions. The act was implemented due to the efforts of social reformer Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar, who strongly advocated for widow remarriage and campaigned for its legalization. This act marked a significant step in India’s social reform movements.

Extra Facts:
☛ The act allowed widows to remarry and restored their property rights.
☛ It was primarily enforced in Bengal, Bombay, and Madras Presidencies.
☛ Before this law, Hindu widows were not permitted to remarry and faced severe social restrictions.
☛ This act paved the way for other social reform laws like the Child Marriage Restraint Act (1929) and the Hindu Marriage Act (1955).
